about: Syllable forms and the rules on what may stand where. A language draws a complexity class, then the forms of that class with their weights. See README.md.
sources: WALS 12A Syllable Structure (Maddieson): 486 languages; simple (C)V: 61, moderately complex (C)(C)V(C) with a limited second onset consonant: 274, complex: 151.

Sonority Sequencing Principle: Clements, G. N. 1990. The role of the sonority cycle in core syllabification. Papers in Laboratory Phonology I, 283-333; Selkirk, E. 1984. On the major class features and syllable theory.
Word length of roots: rough shares, set by hand (no single source).

forms.note: The coda is a nasal only.
A long vowel, or a vowel and a glide (j, w).
The second onset sound is a glide (j, w).
s and a stop: the usual exception to sonority sequencing.
Only s, a stop and a liquid or glide.

formsNote: C any consonant, V a vowel, N a nasal, G a glide (j w), L a liquid (l ʎ ɾ r ɹ), O an obstruent (stop, affricate, fricative), P a stop, s the sound s. A language takes all forms of its class with the weights above, and keeps a random share (0.6 to 1.0) of the forms other than V and CV.

sonority.scale: sounds.json 'sonority': stop 1, affricate 2, fricative 3, nasal 4, tap/trill/lateral 5, approximant 6, vowel 7. Voiced obstruents count +0.5.
sonority.note: In an onset, each sound has a sonority higher than the one before it by at least minDistance; in a coda, lower than the one before it. The exceptions are the onsets of the forms sCV, sCVC, CCCV, CCCVC.

constraints.rule: two equal consonants do not stand in one onset or one coda
an onset of two consonants at the same place does not occur, except stop + liquid at alveolar (tr, dr)
ŋ does not start a word
h and ʔ do not end a syllable
j and w do not end a syllable, except as part of the nucleus (form CVV)
j does not stand before i, w does not stand before u
two vowels do not stand next to each other across a syllable edge
a language draws the consonants that may end a syllable: all, or the sonorants only, or nasals only

rootLengthNote: The syllables of a lexicon root. Short words make compounds that do not get too long; the language may shift the weights (one value, 'wordLength', drawn per language).
